snippets.output: Conjunctival icterus and dark urine suggest hemolysis. Fatigue and low hemoglobin indicate anemia. Elevated bilirubin and LDH levels support hemolysis.
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole can trigger hemolysis in patients with G6PD deficiency. The medication triggers hemolysis due to oxidative stress.
G6PD deficiency is an X-linked recessive disorder that predisposes red blood cells to oxidative damage, leading to hemolytic anemia.
Oxidative damage to red blood cells in G6PD deficiency can lead to the formation of Heinz bodies. These damaged cells can result in 'bite cells' or 'degmacytes' on a peripheral blood smear.
The most likely finding on a peripheral blood smear in this patient is degmacytes (bite cells). The correct answer is degmacytes (bite cells).
